title: The sweep-exclusion pin covers only the due-SELECT; the sweep's claim/advance write boundary never re-checks taken_over_at, so a take-over landing mid-tick still delivers one invite/reminder and mints a token on the taken-over row
detail: taken_over_row_is_excluded_from_the_sweep_test (line 287-306) pins that sweep_due_reference_calls never RETURNS a taken-over row — true, but that filter is selection-time only. The sweep is send-then-claim (sweep.gleam step_t0: send.send_invite(...) then sql.sweep_claim_t0; step_co_nudge/step_reminder likewise send then sql.sweep_advance). Take-over (take_over_reference_call.sql) writes only taken_over_at + next_attempt_at, never status or attempt_count, so if the landlord's take-over commits after the due-SELECT but before/while the send runs, the invite/reminder still goes out to a referee the landlord is now handling personally (A7 'the sweep stops sending' / UX §7.7 'automated contact ceases' violated in the race window), and the guarded claim still SUCCEEDS because sweep_claim_t0's guard is (status='queued' AND attempt_count=0) and sweep_advance's is (status='contact_initiated' AND attempt_count=$4) — neither references taken_over_at. The claim then flips the row to contact_initiated with a minted form_token (next_attempt_at stays NULL, so no further ticks — harm is bounded to the in-flight tick). The test's 'belt and braces' comment implies the exclusion is enforced at the write boundary too; it is not, and no test covers a take-over racing an in-flight tick.
evidence: reference_checks_actions_integration_test.gleam:302 rc_sql.sweep_due_reference_calls(...) (SELECT-only pin); sweep.gleam:324-333 send.send_invite then sql.sweep_claim_t0; sweep_claim_t0.sql:30 WHERE status='queued' AND attempt_count=0 (no taken_over_at IS NULL); sweep_advance.sql:23-24 WHERE status='contact_initiated' AND attempt_count=$4 (no taken_over_at IS NULL); take_over_reference_call.sql SET taken_over_at=now(), next_attempt_at=NULL (status untouched)

title: The AD-7 second-failure exhaustion GATE (correction_cycles >= 1 routing at the delivery webhooks and the wrong-person route) is unpinned — the story's exhaustion test drives the SQL terminal directly, so a regression that flips or drops the gate passes the entire suite
detail: second_failure_exhausts_to_unreachable_with_signal_test (491-540) exercises the exhaustion END of the pipeline: it sets awaiting_correction, runs correct_reference_call, then calls rc_sql.exhaust_reference_call + rc_sql.stamp_referee_contact_invalid directly. The decision that makes the mechanism LIVE — webhooks.gleam apply_delivery_failure `case row.correction_cycles >= 1 { True -> exhaust_row ... False -> mark_awaiting_correction }` and form_handler.gleam apply_wrong_person's identical branch — is covered by no test: no integration test delivers a second failure event through either call site against a row with correction_cycles=1, and the wrong-person exhaustion path (exhaust_wrong_person: stamp + ReferenceCallCorrectionExhausted audit + notify_reference_correction_exhausted in-app notification) has zero coverage on either branch. The pre-existing webhooks suite pins only the first-failure False branch (resend_bounce_moves_row_to_awaiting_correction_test). The gate is correct in the current code (verified by reading both call sites), but the story's 'the rc3-7 mechanism goes LIVE here' acceptance criterion rests on code reading alone: a change flipping the gate to `>= 0`, removing the branch, or skipping the stamp at either call site would leave every test green.
